definition: to stop developing or making progress; to become inactive

collocations.example: Sales began to stagnate once the newer models reached the stores.
Without fresh investment, the economy will stagnate for several years.

definition: a fully grown male horse

collocations.example: The ranch owner proudly showed us his powerful black stallion.
She trains an Arabian stallion for the regional riding competition.

definition: physical or mental strength to keep doing something for a long time

collocations.example: Daily running helped him build up the stamina for a marathon.
The long mountain hike was a real test of our stamina.

definition: to speak with difficulty, repeating sounds or pausing because of nerves or a speech problem

collocations.example: He began to stammer an apology when the manager walked in.
She started to stammer with nerves during the job interview.

definition: a common dark bird with shiny feathers that often gathers in large groups

collocations.example: A huge flock of starlings swirled above the empty field at dusk.
The common starling often nests in holes under the roof.

definition: a person or shop that sells paper, pens, and other writing materials

collocations.example: I bought envelopes and ink at the local stationer this morning.
The stationer's shop on the corner also sells greeting cards.

definition: to keep something bad away or delay it from happening (usually "stave off")

collocations.example: A small snack helped her stave off hunger until dinner.
The emergency loan helped the firm stave off bankruptcy for now.

definition: a ship that is driven by steam power

collocations.example: We crossed the wide lake aboard an old paddle steamer.
The passenger steamer sailed between the two coastal towns daily.

definition: a strong and very unpleasant smell

collocations.example: The stench of rotting food filled the abandoned kitchen.
A foul stench rose from the blocked drain in the yard.

definition: a person whose job is to buy and sell shares for other people

collocations.example: She followed her stockbroker's advice and sold the shares early.
He worked as a stockbroker in the city for ten years.

definition: to collect and store a large supply of something for future use

collocations.example: Hospitals began to stockpile supplies before the busy winter season.
Families rushed to stockpile food ahead of the coming storm.

definition: (of a person) short and solidly built

collocations.example: The security guard had a short, stocky build.
A stocky man in a gray coat blocked the narrow doorway.

definition: not showing feelings, staying calm when facing pain or trouble

collocations.example: She remained stoic as the doctor explained the difficult news.
He bore the long delay in stoic silence without complaint.

definition: to walk with heavy, noisy steps, often because you are angry

collocations.example: The boy stomped off to his room after losing the game.
He stomped around the kitchen, slamming cupboard doors in frustration.

definition: to put something away neatly in a place until it is needed

collocations.example: Passengers must stow luggage safely before the plane takes off.
She helped stow the equipment neatly in the back of the van.

definition: to sit or stand with one leg on each side of something

collocations.example: He turned the chair around and straddled it to face us.
She straddled her bike and waited for the light to change.

definition: to move along slowly in a loose, untidy group, falling behind others

collocations.example: A few tired hikers began to straggle behind the main group.
The children straggled along the path, stopping to look at everything.

definition: layers of rock or earth lying one on top of another

collocations.example: The cliff showed colorful rock strata formed over millions of years.
Geologists studied the sedimentary strata along the river valley.

definition: a flat frame used to carry a sick or injured person

collocations.example: The injured player was carried off on a stretcher.
Paramedics lifted him onto the ambulance stretcher with great care.

definition: seriously affected by something unpleasant such as trouble or disaster

collocations.example: Aid workers rushed food into the flood-stricken area.
The grief-stricken family gathered quietly at the hospital.

definition: angry disagreement or conflict between people or groups

collocations.example: Internal strife within the party weakened its chances in the election.
Money problems often cause strife between close friends.

definition: to speak with difficulty, repeating the first sounds of words

collocations.example: He began to stutter nervously when the teacher called his name.
She stuttered over the word and had to start the sentence again.

definition: to pay another company to do part of the work you have agreed to do

collocations.example: The builder decided to subcontract the electrical work to a local firm.
They subcontract production to several small factories overseas.

definition: words shown on screen that write out or translate what is said in a film or show

collocations.example: I turned on the subtitles to follow the fast dialogue.
The foreign film was shown with clear English subtitles.

definition: said clearly in a few words; brief and to the point

collocations.example: She gave a succinct summary of the report in two minutes.
His succinct answer left no room for confusion.

definition: a person who is easily fooled or cheated

collocations.example: They tricked him into paying twice, and he felt like a real sucker.
Don't take me for a sucker; I know the real price.

definition: the right to vote in political elections

collocations.example: The movement campaigned for universal suffrage for all adults.
Women's suffrage was finally granted after years of protest.

definition: to be silent and bad-tempered because you are annoyed about something

collocations.example: He sat and sulked in silence after the argument.
She sulked about missing the party for the rest of the day.

definition: silently bad-tempered or gloomy

collocations.example: The teenager gave her parents a sullen look and said nothing.
The team drove home in sullen silence after the loss.

definition: expensive and looking grand; luxurious

collocations.example: The hotel served a sumptuous feast for the wedding guests.
We dined in sumptuous surroundings at the old palace.

definition: to place one thing over another so that both can be seen

collocations.example: You can superimpose the logo onto the photo in minutes.
The designer superimposed an image of the building over the map.

definition: a belief that certain actions or things bring good or bad luck

collocations.example: According to superstition, walking under a ladder brings bad luck.
An old superstition says a broken mirror means seven unlucky years.

definition: to take the place of someone or something else

collocations.example: The new manager quickly supplanted his older rival at the firm.
Digital tickets have largely supplanted the old paper system.

definition: bending easily; not stiff

collocations.example: Gentle stretching exercises help keep your body supple.
The cream leaves your skin feeling soft and supple.

definition: the family name shared by members of a family

collocations.example: Smith is a very common surname in England.
Could you please spell your surname for the form?

definition: a feeling of excited or anxious uncertainty about what will happen

collocations.example: The last chapter kept readers in suspense until the very end.
The long wait for the results was almost unbearable suspense.

definition: a warm, loose cotton top with long sleeves

collocations.example: He wore a gray hooded sweatshirt to the gym.
She pulled on a soft cotton sweatshirt against the morning chill.

definition: pigs, especially as farm animals

collocations.example: The farmer raises swine and cattle on his land.
A herd of swine rooted in the mud near the barn.

definition: a soft rushing or hissing sound made by movement through air or water

collocations.example: She left the room with a quick swish of her skirt.
We heard the gentle swish of water against the boat.

definition: a building where Jewish people meet for worship

collocations.example: Many families attend the synagogue on Saturday mornings.
The old synagogue in the city center dates back centuries.

definition: relating to the way words are arranged to form sentences

collocations.example: The essay used a limited range of syntactic structures.
The software performs a syntactic analyzis of each sentence.

definition: the rules for arranging words to make correct sentences

collocations.example: English syntax usually places the subject before the verb.
Her grammar and syntax improved after months of practice.

definition: a scene formed by a group of people or objects arranged in a striking way

collocations.example: The parade included a colorful tableau of a famous historical battle.
She paused to watch the peaceful domestic tableau by the fire.

definition: to touch or change something without permission, often causing damage

collocations.example: Never tamper with the safety controls on the machine.
He was accused of trying to tamper with the evidence.

definition: two people or things working together (usually "in tandem")

collocations.example: The two departments worked in tandem to finish the project.
The new rules were introduced in tandem with a training program.

definition: a strong, sharp taste or smell

collocations.example: She could smell the salty tang of the sea air.
The sauce had a sharp tang of lemon and ginger.

definition: a sudden outburst of bad temper, especially by a child

collocations.example: The toddler threw a tantrum when it was time to leave.
He had a temper tantrum because his plan was rejected.

definition: the paved area at an airport where planes stand or move

collocations.example: Two planes stood on the tarmac waiting to take off.
Passengers waited on the tarmac during the long delay.

definition: to damage someone's good reputation or image

collocations.example: The scandal could tarnish the company's good reputation.
One careless remark tarnished his public image overnight.

definition: a message sent by telegraph and delivered in printed form

collocations.example: She went to the office to send an urgent telegram.
He received a telegram announcing his brother's arrival.

definition: very weak or slight; not strong or certain

collocations.example: The report found only a tenuous link between the two events.
Her tenuous argument failed to convince the committee.

definition: a small insect that eats wood and can damage buildings

collocations.example: The inspector found serious termite damage in the old floor.
A tall termite mound rose from the dry grassland.

definition: a rope or chain used to tie an animal to one spot

collocations.example: The goat was tied to a post with a long tether.
The dog ran in circles on its tether in the yard.

definition: straw or reeds used as a material to make a roof

collocations.example: The cottage had a thick thatch roof that kept out the rain.
A craftsman came to repair the thatch on the old barn.

definition: a statement in mathematics that has been proved to be true

collocations.example: It took the student hours to prove the theorem.
The lesson explained a famous mathematical theorem step by step.

definition: in that place, document, or thing (formal)

collocations.example: The contract and the rules contained therein must be followed.
He works very hard, and therein lies the key to his success.

definition: an instrument used to measure temperature

collocations.example: The nurse read the thermometer and noted the temperature.
She used a digital thermometer to check the baby's fever.

definition: a group of bushes or small trees growing closely together

collocations.example: The rabbit vanished into a dense thicket beside the path.
The birds like to hide in the thicket near the pond.

definition: the state of being completely controlled or fascinated by someone or something

collocations.example: The crowd was in thrall to the speaker's powerful voice.
The magician held the whole audience in thrall.

definition: a group of three people

collocations.example: The three friends played golf as a threesome every Sunday.
The sisters formed a happy threesome throughout their childhood.

definition: a herb with small leaves used to add flavor to food

collocations.example: She added fresh thyme to the roasting vegetables.
Place a sprig of thyme on top of the chicken before baking.

definition: a gland in the neck that controls growth and the use of energy

collocations.example: The doctor examined her thyroid gland during the check-up.
Constant tiredness can sometimes signal a thyroid problem.

definition: the shape and physical features of the land in an area

collocations.example: The map clearly showed the local topography of the valley.
The region's rugged topography makes road building difficult.

definition: a long underwater missile fired at ships

collocations.example: The submarine prepared to fire a torpedo at the target.
A torpedo struck the side of the warship and it began to sink.

definition: a slow-moving land animal with a hard shell

collocations.example: The zoo's giant tortoise is over a hundred years old.
The pattern on the tortoise shell was beautifully marked.

definition: describing a government that controls everything and allows no opposition

collocations.example: People had no free speech under the totalitarian regime.
Art served only the leaders in the totalitarian state.

definition: the grip of a tire or wheel on the surface it moves over

collocations.example: The car lost traction on the icy mountain road.
These winter tires give good traction on wet surfaces.

definition: a sleep-like state in which someone is not fully aware of their surroundings

collocations.example: He stared out of the window as if in a trance.
The hypnotist helped her fall into a deep trance.

definition: a small electronic part that controls the flow of electric current

collocations.example: My grandfather still keeps his old transistor radio.
The engineer replaced a faulty power transistor in the circuit.

definition: allowing light to pass through but not fully transparent

collocations.example: The roof was made of translucent plastic that softened the light.
The bathroom window used translucent glass for privacy.

definition: to happen, or to become known as the facts come out

collocations.example: It later transpired that the report had been wrong.
Several problems transpired during the meeting yesterday.

definition: a long, formal piece of writing about a particular subject

collocations.example: The scholar spent years writing a treatise on education.
She published a famous treatise on human rights.

definition: to become, or to make something, three times as large

collocations.example: The town's population has trebled in size over twenty years.
Rising demand trebled the amount of stock they usually kept.

definition: a slight shaking movement, especially of the body or the ground

collocations.example: There was a slight tremor in his hands as he signed.
A small earth tremor shook the buildings early this morning.

definition: something of little value or importance

collocations.example: The repair cost was a mere trifle compared to a new car.
Don't waste your time worrying over such trifles.

definition: an imaginary creature in old stories, often large and ugly, living in caves or under bridges

collocations.example: The story told of a troll hiding under the old stone bridge.
In the tale, an ugly troll guarded the mountain path.

definition: a group of performers who work and travel together

collocations.example: The dance troupe will give three shows this week.
The small theater troupe toured the villages every summer.

definition: able to be trusted; reliable and honest

collocations.example: Everyone saw her as a calm and trustworthy leader.
We need a business partner who is honest and trustworthy.

definition: the stomach (informal)

collocations.example: The child stayed home with a bad tummy ache.
She ate too much cake and got a sore tummy.

definition: a state of loud noise and confusion among a crowd of people

collocations.example: The whole city was in tumult after the shocking news.
A tumult of voices rose from the crowded square.

definition: a cold, flat region where no trees grow and the ground is frozen

collocations.example: Few plants survive on the frozen arctic tundra.
The herd moved slowly across the open tundra.

definition: a loose garment, usually reaching to the knees, worn over the body

collocations.example: He wore a long brown tunic tied at the waist.
The guard stood at the gate in a simple tunic.

definition: a greenish-blue color

collocations.example: The sea was an improbably pale turquoise under the sun.
She painted the bedroom walls a soft turquoise blue.

definition: a small tower on the corner of a building, especially a castle

collocations.example: A flag flew from the highest castle turret.
The old house had a round turret at one corner.

definition: to make small changes to something in order to improve it

collocations.example: He tweaked the settings until the photo looked right.
You may need to tweak the figures before the meeting.

definition: to spin around quickly, or to make something spin

collocations.example: The dancer twirled around gracefully on the stage.
She tends to twirl her hair when she feels nervous.

definition: to be a typical example of something

collocations.example: These two buildings typify the local building style.
The painting seems to typify the fashions of that era.

definition: a cruel ruler who uses power unfairly

collocations.example: The country was ruled for years by a cruel tyrant.
The people finally rose up to overthrow the tyrant.

definition: a medical scan that uses high-frequency sound waves to see inside the body

collocations.example: She had an ultrasound scan during her pregnancy.
The ultrasound showed that she was expecting twins.

definition: to emphasise something or show that it is important

collocations.example: The report underscores the importance of regular saving.
She used real examples to underscore her main point.

definition: to move or lie in smooth, wave-like curves

collocations.example: The green hills undulate gently toward the distant coast.
The fields of wheat undulate like waves in the wind.

definition: to find something by digging it out of the ground

collocations.example: The workers unearthed buried treasure beneath the old wall.
Archaeologists unearthed an ancient tomb near the river.

definition: forming a single or united whole, with power held centrally

collocations.example: The country runs on a unitary system with one central government.
Power in a unitary state rests mainly with the national government.

definition: difficult to control; disorderly

collocations.example: He ran his fingers through his thick, unruly hair.
Police struggled to calm the unruly crowd outside.

definition: happening soon; about to take place

collocations.example: Both parties are preparing for the upcoming election.
The poster listed every upcoming event at the hall.

definition: a loud noise or an angry public reaction

collocations.example: The surprise announcement caused an uproar in the crowd.
The whole office was in an uproar over the new rules.
